speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; how many days postpartum are you, and has your delivery been vaginal or cesarean?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your vaginal delivery, prolonged labor, and symptoms of urinary frequency and uterine tenderness, I need to rule out puerperal endometritis and a urinary tract infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture. How many days postpartum are you, and has your fever been continuous or intermittent?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Puerperal Endometritis

I understand you are experiencing fever, uterine tenderness, urinary frequency, and decreased bowel sounds. While the symptoms you described strongly suggest a postpartum infection like endometritis, I cannot ignore the "decreased bowel sounds" as they may indicate an associated pelvic abscess or ileus. Have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? Additionally, have you had any pain during urination?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Blood Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
